A.notes: The brick-and-courtyard idea is strong and the project pairings of image plus plan fit the brief well; the palette, numbering and drawing language give it a distinct studio signature. But the default-motion version appears to lose the main hero statement almost entirely, and the scroll-frame strip suggests mostly straightforward section progression rather than motion that adds meaning. Reduced motion is handled better than the animated state, which hurts both craft and motion.

B.notes: This is the clearer and more complete interpretation on first read: the positioning statement, plan motif and warm brick/light palette all show up immediately and stay consistent through the site. The motion evidence looks modest—mainly orderly reveal/progression between sections rather than a rich spatial sequence—but it serves the content and does not seem to break it. Overall it is less surprising than A, but more resolved and dependable.

raw.why: B presents the brief more completely and cleanly, while A’s more original direction is undermined by a broken-looking motion/default hero state.
